spans.s:
भदन्त भदन्त, भदाक. See under rt.
भन्द् below.

भदन्त, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. भण्ड्,
col. 1), a term of respect applied to a Buddhist; a
Buddhist mendicant.
—भदन्त-गोप-देव and
भदन्त-गोषक or भदन्त-घोषक, अस्, m.,
N. of two Buddhist teachers.
—भदन्त-ज्ञान-
वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a poet.
—भदन्त-धर्म-
त्रात and भदन्त-राम, अस्, m., N. of two Bud-
dhist teachers.
—भदन्त-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a
poet.
—भदन्त-श्री-लाभ, अस्, m., N. of a Bud-
dhist teacher (also called Śrī-lābha).
भद्र भद्र. See under rt. भन्द् below.

भद्र, अस्, आ, अम्, good, well, prosperous,
happy, auspicious (e. g. भद्रा दिश्, the auspicious
quarter, the south); favourable, propitious, gracious,
kind, friendly, benevolent, pious, excellent, (भद्रो
नृपतिः, a good or gracious king; often used
in voc. sing. m. भद्र as a familiar mode of
address, in the sense of ‘my good sir,’ ‘my dear
fellow;’ and in voc. sing. f. भद्रे, ‘my good
lady,’ ‘my dear madam’); pleasant, enjoyable,
desirable, laudable, commendable; lovely, beauti-
ful; beloved, dear; specious, plausible, hypocritical,
any hypocrite or impostor, (according to Kullūka on
Manu

= कल्याणाचार-प्रच्छन्न-पाप);
(अम्), n. prosperity, happiness, welfare, good fortune,
fortune, (भद्राणि, n. pl. = भद्रम्, good for-
tune; भद्रम् अ-व्याहतम्, uninterrupted happi-
ness or prosperity; भद्रं ते, prosperity to thee!
भद्रं वः, happiness to you! may it be well
with you! frequently mere forms politely used in
conversation, and sometimes equivalent to our expres-
sions ‘if you please,’ ‘with all deference or respect
for you,’ &c.); gold; iron, steel; a fragrant grass,
Cyperus Rotundus [cf. भद्र-मुस्त]; a particular
[]
posture in sitting (= भद्रासन); N. of the
seventh of the eleven astronomical periods called
Karaṇas; of various Sāmans; (अस्), m. a bullock; a
term applied to a particular kind of elephant; N. of
one of the elephants which support the world; a
water wag-tail [cf. भद्र-नामन्]; a heap, multi-
tude (?); Nauclea Cadamba; Tithymalus Antiquorum;
an epithet of Śiva; N. of one of the twelve sons of
Viṣṇu and one of the Tuṣita deities in the Svā-
yambhava Manv-antara; (with Jainas) N. of the
third of the nine white Balas; N. of a son of Vasu-
deva and Pauravī; of a son of Vasu-deva and Devakī;
of a son of Upacāru-mat; of an actor; of a friend
of Bāṇa; of a son of Kṛṣṇa; an epithet of mount
Meru; (with Buddhists) N. of a particular world;
(आस्), m. pl., N. of a class of divinities under the
third Manu; N. of a people; (आ), f. a cow; N.
of various plants (= कृष्णा, अनन्ता, रास्ना,
प्र-सारिणी, जीवन्ती, अपराजिता, नीली, बला,
शमी, वचा, दन्ती, हरिद्रा, श्वेत-दूर्वा, काश्-
मरी, सारिवा-विशेष, काकोडुम्बरिका); Gmelina
Arborea; a kind of metre, the first and third lines
of which are ˘¯˘¯¯˘˘¯˘¯¯, and the second
and fourth ¯¯˘¯¯ &c.; N. of the second, seventh,
and twelfth days of the lunar fortnight; of a goddess;
of a Buddhist woman; of Dākṣāyaṇī in Bhadre-
śvara; of a Vidyā-dharī; of a daughter of Surabhi;
of a wife of Vasu-deva; of the wife of Vaiśravaṇa;
of a daughter of Soma and wife of Utathya; of a
daughter of Raudrāśva and the Apsaras Ghṛtācī; of
a Kākṣīvatī and wife of Vyuṣitāśva; of a daughter
of Meru and wife of Bhadrāśva; of a daughter of
Sruta-kīrtti and wife of Kṛṣṇa; of various rivers;
of a river described as rising on the northern summit
of Meru and flowing through Uttara-kuru into the
northern ocean; the celestial Ganges; भद्रम्,
भद्रया, भद्रेभिस्, ind., Ved. auspiciously,
favourably, propitiously, happily, well, rightly; [cf.
Lat. fastus for fad-tus, fastigium, fastidium,
festivus: Goth. bats, bat-iza, ‘better;’ bat-ista,
‘best:’ Angl. Sax. bet: Old Germ. baz, ‘better;’
beziro, bezisto, ‘best:’ Goth. ga-bat-non, bot-a,
bot-jan: Angl. Sax. bót: Hib. feodhas, ‘better;’
badhach, ‘famous;’ perhaps maith: Cambro-Brit.
mad, ‘good.’]
—भद्र-कण्ट, अस्, m. the plant
Asteracantha Longifolia.
—भद्र-कन्या, f., N.
of the mother of Maudgalyāyana.
—भद्र-कपिल,
अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva; [cf. भद्र and कपिल.]
—भद्र-कर्णिका, f., N. of Dākṣāyaṇī in Go-
karṇa.
—भद्र-कर्णेश्वर (˚ण-ईश्˚), N. of a
sacred bathing-place.
—भद्र-कल्प, अस्, m. (with
Buddhists) ‘the good or beautiful Kalpa,’ N. of the
present age; of a Sūtra work.
—भद्रकल्पिक,
अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva.
—भद्र-कार, अस्,
m., N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a
people.
—भद्र-कारक, अस्, इका, अम्, causing
prosperity or welfare, propitious, prosperous.
—भ-
द्र-काली, f., N. of a goddess; (in the later mytho-
logy) a form of Durgā [cf. Manu
III. 89

]; N. of
one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda; a species
of plant (= गन्धोली); N. of a village on the
right bank of the Ganges.
—भद्रकाली-क-
वच, अम्, n., N. of the thirty-seventh chapter of
the Gaṇeśa-khaṇḍa or third part of the Brahma-
vaivarta-Purāṇa.
—भद्रकाली-पूजा-यन्त्र, अम्,
n., N. of a mystical diagram mentioned in Kṛṣṇā-
nanda's Tantra-sāra.
—भद्रकाली-मनु, उस्, m.,
N. of the ninth chapter of the Pheṭ-kāriṇī-tantra.
—भद्रकाली-मन्त्र, आस्, m. pl., N. of a chapter
of the Tantra-sāra.
—भद्र-काशी, f. = भद्र-
मुस्ता, q. v.
—भद्र-काष्ठ, अम्, n. the wood
of Pinus Deodora or of Pinus Longifolia.
—भद्र-
कुम्भ, अस्, m. ‘auspicious jar,’ a golden jar filled
with water from a holy place or from the Ganges
(used especially at the consecration of a king).
—भद्र-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. causing prosperity or
welfare; (with Jainas) N. of the twenty-fourth Arhat
of the future Ut-sarpiṇī.
—भद्र-गणित, अम्, n.
the construction of magical squares or diagrams.
—भद्र-गन्धिका, f. the plant Cyperus Rotun-
dus (= मुस्तक); the creeping plant Asclepias Pseu-
[]
dosarsa.
—भद्र-गौर, अस्, m., N. of a mountain.
—भद्र-घट or भद्र-घटक, अस्, m. a
vessel from which a lottery is drawn.
—भद्रङ्-
कर, अस्, ई, अम्, auspicious, propitious, causing pros-
perity or happiness; (अस्), m., N. of a person;
(अम्), n., N. of a town in Vidarbha.
—भद्रङ्-
करण, अस्, ई, अम्, causing prosperity or happiness,
prosperous.
—भद्र-चारु, उस्, m., N. of a son of
Kṛṣṇa.
—भद्र-चूड, अस्, m. the plant Euphor-
bia Tirucalli.
—भद्र-ज, अस्, m. the plant Wrightia
Antidysenterica.
—भद्र-जय, अस्, m., N. of a
man.
—भद्र-जानि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having a beau-
tiful wife.
—भद्र-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more pros-
perous, happier; better.
—भद्र-तरुणी, f. the
plant Trapa Bispinosa (= कुब्जक).
—भद्र-ता,
f. or भद्र-त्व, अम्, n. honesty, probity; pros-
perity, good fortune.
—भद्र-तुङ्ग, N. of a
sacred bathing-place.
—भद्र-तुरग, अम्, n., N.
of a Varṣa.
—भद्र-दन्त, अस्, m., N. of an
elephant.
—भद्र-दन्तिका, f. a species of Croton.
—भद्र-दारु, उस्, उ, m. n. a sort of pine, Pinus
Deodora; Pinus Longifolia.
—भद्रदार्व्-आदिक,
अस्, m. a class of thirty-nine medicinal plants and
substances.
—भद्र-देह, अस्, m., N. of a son of
Kṛṣṇa.
—भद्र-द्वीप, अस्, m., N. of an island.
—भद्र-नामन्, आ, m. the wood-pecker; the
water wag-tail; [cf. भद्र.]
—भद्र-नामिका,
f. a species of plant (= त्रायमाणा).
—भद्र-
निधि, इस्, m. ‘treasure of fortune,’ a term applied
to a costly vessel offered to Viṣṇu.
—भद्र-
पद, अम्, n. a kind of metre; (आ), f., N. of the
third and fourth lunar asterisms (= प्रोष्ठ-पद;
cf. नक्षत्र).
—भद्रपदा-योग, अस्, m.,
N. of the twenty-eighth chapter of Bhaṭṭotpala's
commentary on Varāha-mihira's Bṛhat-saṃhitā.
—भद्र-पर्णा, f. the shrub Pæderia Fœtida.
—भद्र-पर्णी, f. the tree Gmelina Arborea; the
shrub Pæderia Fœtida.
—भद्रपाद, अस्, ई, अम्,
born under the Nakṣatra Bhadra-padā.
—भद्र-
पाल, अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva.
—भद्र-पी-
ठ, अम्, n. a beautiful chair, splendid seat, throne;
a kind of winged insect, (perhaps incorrectly for a
form भद्र-कीट.)
—भद्र-पुर, अम्, n., N. of
a city; [cf. भद्रा-नगर.]
—भद्र-बलन,
अस्, m. = बल-भद्र, N. of the elder brother of
Kṛṣṇa.
—भद्र-बला, f. the shrub Pæderia Fœ-
tida; Sida Cordifolia (= बला).
—भद्र-बाहु,
उस्, m., N. of a son of Vasu-deva by Rohiṇī (Pau-
ravī); of a king of Magadha; (with Jainas) N. of
one of the six Śruta-kevalins; of the author of certain
Kalpa-sūtras; of the author of the Jātakāmbho-nidhi;
(ऊस्), f., N. of a woman.
—भद्रबाहु-शास्त्र, अम्,
n., N. of a work mentioned in Nārāyaṇa's Praśnār-
ṇava.
—भद्रबाहु-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of an author
mentioned in Cāritra-siṃha-gaṇi's Shaḍdarśana-vṛtti.
—भद्र-भुज, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘auspicious-armed,’
whose arms confer prosperity.
—भद्र-भूषणी,
f., N. of a deity.
—भद्र-मनस्, आस्, f., N. of
the mother of the elephant Airāvata; [cf. भद्र-
रेणु.]
—भद्र-मन्द, अस्, m. epithet of a parti-
cular kind of elephant; (also read भद्र-मन्द्र;
cf. भद्र, मन्द, मन्द्र.)
—भद्रमन्द्र-
मृग, अस्, m. epithet of a particular kind of ele-
phant.
—भद्र-मल्लिका, f. a species of plant, Cu-
cumis Madraspatanus (= गवाक्षी).
—भद्र-मा-
तृ, ता, f. a good or beautiful mother.
—भद्र-
मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, one whose face (i. e. whose
look) confers prosperity; (अस्), m., N. of a Nāga.
—भद्र-मुञ्ज, अस्, m. a plant akin to Saccha-
rum Sara.
—भद्र-मुस्त or भद्र-मुस्ता, f. a
variety of Cyperus.
—भद्रमुस्तक, अस्, m. =
भद्र-मुस्त.
—भद्र-मृग, अस्, m. epithet
of a particular kind of elephant.
—भद्र-यव,
अम्, n. the seed of Wrightia Antidysenterica (=
इन्द्र-यव).
—भद्र-यान, अस्, m., N. of a
man; (commonly written भद्रायन.)
—भ-
द्रयानीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of the school founded by
Bhadra-yāna; (commonly written भद्रायनीय.)
—भद्र-योग, अस्, m., N. of a subdivision of the
Purāṇa-sarvasva; of an astrological Yoga.
—भद्र-
रथ, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—भद्र-रुचि, इस्,
[]
m., N. of a man.
—भद्र-रूपा, f., N. of a
woman.
—भद्र-रेणु, उस्, m., N. of Indra's ele-
phant; (also read भद्र-वेणु; cf. भद्र-म-
नस्.)
—भद्र-रोहिणी, f. a species of plant.
—भ-
द्र-वट, अस्, m. ‘the auspicious or beautiful fig-
tree,’ N. of a place.
—भद्र-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
fraught with good, auspicious; (अती), f. a wanton,
courtezan (?Ved.); the tree Gmelia Arborea; N. of
a daughter of Kṛṣṇa; of a wife of Madhu (with
the patronymic Pauravī); N. of a female elephant;
(अत्), n. the tree Pinus Deodora; N. of a Tīrtha.
—भद्र-वर्मन्, आ, m. ‘Double Arabian Jasmine,’
N. of a man.
—भद्र-वल्लिका, f. the plant Hemi-
desmus Indicus.
—भद्र-वल्ली, f. Jasminum Sam-
bac; Gærtnera Racemosa, a large Bengal creeper;
the plant Vallaris Dichotomus.
—भद्र-वसन,
अम्, n. splendid apparel, magnificent array.
—भ-
द्र-वाच्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. speaking auspiciously.
—भ-
द्र-वाच्य, अम्, n., Ved. wishing well, congratu-
lation.
—भद्र-वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. uttering
auspicious cries (said of a bird).
—भद्र-विन्द,
अस्, m., N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa.
—भद्र-विराज्,
ट्, f. a kind of metre.
—भद्र-विहार, अस्, m., N.
of a Buddhist monastery.
—भद्र-वेणु, another
form for भद्र-रेणु, q. v.
—भद्र-व्रात, अस्,
आ, अम्, Ved. having or forming a happy assem-
blage.
—भद्र-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a man with
the patronymic Kauśika; [cf. भाद्रशर्मि.]
—भ-
द्र-शाख, अस्, m., N. of a form of Skanda.
—भद्र-शाल-वन = भद्र-साल-वन, q. v.
—भद्र-शील, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—भद्र-
शोचि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. beautifully shining, flashing,
coruscating, glittering.
—भद्र-शौनक, अस्, m.,
N. of a man.
—भद्र-श्रय or भद्र-श्रिय,
अम्, n. sandal-wood.
—भद्र-श्रवस्, आस्, m., N.
of a son of Dharma.
—भद्र-श्री, ईस्, f. the
sandal tree.
—भद्र-श्रुत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. hearing
good, hearing pleasant things.
—भद्र-श्रेण्य, अस्,
m., N. of a king.
—भद्र-षष्ठी, f., N. of a
form of Durgā.
—भद्र-सामन्, आ, m., N. of a
man.
—भद्र-सार, अस्, m., N. of a king; (also
read विन्दु-सार.)
—भद्र-साल-वन, (probably)
अम्, n., N. of a forest (of fine Shorea Robusta trees).
—भद्र-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a man with the
patronymic Ajātaśatrava; of a son of Vasu-deva and
Devakī; of a son of Ṛṣabha; of a son of Mahiṣ-
mat, (in this sense also भद्रसेनक); N. of a
king of Kaśmīra; (with Buddhists) N. of the leader
of the host of the evil spirit Māra-pāpīyas.
—भ-
द्र-सोमा, f., N. of a river in Uttara-kuru; a N. of
the Ganges.
—भद्र-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
beautiful-handed, auspicious-handed (said of the
Aśvins).
—भद्रा-करण, अम्, n. ‘making beau-
tiful,’ the act of shaving.
—भद्रा-कृ, cl. 8. P.
-करोति, -कर्तुम्, ‘to make beautiful,’ to shave;
[cf. मद्रा-कृ.]
—भद्राक्ष (˚र-अक्˚), अस्,
m. ‘fair-eyed,’ N. of a king [cf. भल्लाक्ष]; a
particular seed of which beads are made (?).
—भ-
द्राङ्ग (˚र-अङ्˚), अस्, m. ‘beauteous-framed,’ having
a handsome person,’ an epithet of Bala-bhadra.
—भ-
द्रात्मज (˚र-आत्˚), अस्, m. ‘son of iron,’ a sword.
—भद्रा-नगर, अम्, n., N. of a city; [cf. भ-
द्र-पुर.]
—भद्राभद्र (˚र-अभ्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, good and bad; (अम्), n. good and evil.
—भ-
द्रायुध (˚र-आय्˚), अस्, m. ‘handsome-weaponed,’
N. of a giant; of a warrior.
—भद्रायुस् (˚र-आय्˚),
उस्, m., N. of a man.
—भद्रावकाशा (˚र-अव्˚),
f., N. of a sacred river.
—भद्रा-व्रत, अम्, n. a
particular religious ceremony; (also called विष्टि-
व्रत.)
—भद्राश्रम (˚र or ˚रा-आश्˚), अस्, m.,
N. of a hermitage mentioned in the Śambhala-
māhātmya portion of the Skanda-Purāṇa.
—भद्रा-
श्रय, अम्, n. sandal-wood (= भद्र-श्रय, q. v.).
—भद्राश्व (˚र-अश्˚), अस्, m., N. of a Dvīpa said
in the Purāṇas to be named after Bhadrāśva, son of
Āgnīdhra, (some systems describe Bhadrāśva as one
of the four Mahā-dvīpas into which the known world
is divided, while another states it to be one of nine
Khaṇḍas or smaller divisions into which the conti-
nent is distributed; in either case it is the eastern
division); N. of a son of Vasu-deva and Rohiṇī; of
[]
a son of Dhundhumāra; of a king called Bhadrāśva
Śveta-vāhana; of a son of Āgnīdhra or Agnīdhra;
(अम्), n., N. of a Varṣa named after the son of
Āgnīdhra.
—भद्रासन (˚र-आस्˚), अम्, n. a
splendid seat, chair of state, throne; a particular
posture of a devotee while meditating, (the legs being
crossed and bent underneath the body and turned so
as to bring the ankles into contact with the perinæum
while the soles of the feet are held close to the
sides.)
—भद्राह (˚र-अह), अम्, n., Ved. an
auspicious day, favourable season.
—भद्रेन्द्र
(˚र-इन्˚), अस्, m., N. of a man.
—भद्रेश (˚र-
ईश), अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva.
—भद्रेश्वर (˚र-
ईश्˚), अस्, m. an epithet of various statues and Liṅgas
of Śiva; N. of a place; of a Kāyastha.
—भ-
द्रैला (˚र-एला), f. large cardamoms.
—भद्रो-
दनी (˚र-ओद्˚), f. Sida Cordifolia; Uraria Lagopodi-
oides.
—भद्रोदय (˚र-उद्˚), अम्, n., N. of a par-
ticular medicinal compound.

भाद्रदारव, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to or coming
from Bhadra-dāru, q. v.

भाद्रपद, अस्, m. (fr. भद्र-पदा), the
month Bhādra (a rainy month corresponding to a
period in our calendar from about the middle of
August to the middle of September); (आ), f. (also ए,
du., आस्, pl.), = भद्र-पदा, a name common to
the third and fourth lunar asterisms or Nakṣatras
[cf. नक्षत्र]; (ई), f. the day of full moon in the
month Bhādrapada.

भाद्रमातुर, अस्, m. (fr. भद्र-मातृ), the
son of a virtuous or handsome mother.

भाद्रमौञ्ज, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. made from
Bhadra (a kind of Cyperus grass) and Muñja.

भाद्रवर्मण, अस्, m. a patronymic from
Bhadra-varman.

भाद्रशर्मि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Bhadra-
śarman.

भाद्रसाम, अस्, m. a patronymic from Bhadra-
sāman.
